decisions.choice: the first return from exile, led by Zerubbabel and Jeshua
decisions.reason: Zerubbabel, of the royal line of David, and Jeshua the high priest led the first group of exiles home from Babylon after Cyrus allowed it in about 538 BC (Ezra 1:1-4; 2:2; 3:2). The chapter goes back almost a century before Nehemiah's own time to list the priestly and Levite families from then until his day (verse 26).

decisions.choice: Seraiah, Jeremiah, Ezra: heads of priestly families, not the prophet or the scribe
decisions.reason: These names head priestly families of the first return; most of them come back as family names in verses 12-21 and among those who signed the pledge in 10:3-9. This Jeremiah is not the prophet, and this Ezra lived some eighty years before Ezra the scribe, who came to Jerusalem in about 458 BC (Ezra 7:1-8).

decisions.choice: one list running through verse 7
decisions.reason: The list of priests begins here and closes in verse 7 with "these were the heads of the priests". The Literal and Balanced levels end each verse with a comma so the list reads as one sentence.

decisions.choice: came back from exile; The priests were
decisions.reason: "Went up" is the usual word for returning from Babylon to Jerusalem; Readable says what it means and starts the list as its own sentence. Verse 8 begins the Levites.

decisions.choice: passé simple at Literal and Balanced ("montèrent"); passé composé at Readable ("sont revenus")
decisions.reason: For the narrative of this chapter, as in Ezra and the rest of Nehemiah: the passé simple is the tense of written narrative, the passé composé the tense most readers use today. Nehemiah's own account (from verse 31) follows the same rule.

decisions.choice: the list is introduced with a closed sentence ("…다음과 같다") and the names run on with commas to verse 7
alternatives: one Korean sentence ending only in verse 7
decisions.reason: Korean puts the verb last, so the sentence that names the group closes here and the names follow as a list, as the English Literal and Balanced keep the list open across verses 1-7 (m3).

en.B: Bakbukiah and Unni, their fellow Levites, stood opposite them as they served.
en.R: Bakbukiah, Unni, and other Levites stood facing them during worship, and the two groups answered each other in song.

fr.R: Baqbouqia, Ounni et d’autres Lévites se tenaient en face d’eux pendant le culte, et les deux groupes se répondaient en chantant.

ko.R: 박부갸와 운니와 다른 레위 사람들은 예배 때 그들을 마주 보고 섰고, 두 무리가 서로 주고받으며 노래했다.

decisions.choice: opposite them: two groups singing in answer
decisions.reason: The singers stood in two groups facing each other, one answering the other, "division corresponding to division" (verse 24). Ezra 3:11 describes the same kind of answering song at the founding of the temple.

decisions.choice: Unni, as the text is read
decisions.reason: The written consonants of this name differ slightly from the way the text is read; the Masoretes noted the reading in the margin (the qere), and this translation follows it, as the source data does. The person meant is the same either way.

decisions.choice: the two groups answered each other in song
decisions.reason: Readable says what standing opposite meant in worship, from verse 24.

decisions.reason: The short Hebrew form, kept apart from King Jehoiakim ("Joïaqim") as the terms note asks.

decisions.choice: Jonathan, perhaps the Johanan of verses 22-23
decisions.reason: Verses 22-23 name Johanan after Joiada and before Jaddua, and call him "son of Eliashib", perhaps meaning grandson. Jonathan and Johanan are different names, so either the same man is meant and one spelling arose in copying, or the list skips a generation. A Persian-period letter found at Elephantine in Egypt (407 BC) names a high priest Johanan in Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: the next generation, family by family
decisions.reason: Joiakim was the high priest after Jeshua (verse 10). Verses 12-21 go through the priestly families of verses 1-7 in nearly the same order and give the head of each one a generation later: the family name first, then its head.

decisions.choice: heads of the fathers: heads of fathers' houses
decisions.reason: "Fathers" is short for "fathers' houses", the extended families of a clan (see Numbers 1:2).

decisions.choice: of (Balanced); for, led the family of (Readable)
decisions.reason: Each pair is a family and its head; Readable writes out the relation so the list is not mistaken for father and son.

decisions.choice: "en la de Seraías, Meraías" (Balanced), through verse 21
decisions.reason: Balanced makes plain that each pair is a family and its head ("en la [familia] de"), where the English says "for"; Literal keeps the bare "de".

decisions.choice: "họ Sê-ra-gia có Mê-ra-gia" (Balanced), through verse 21
decisions.reason: A bare "của" between two names would read as father and son; Balanced names the family ("họ") and its head ("có"), Readable says "lãnh đạo gia tộc".

decisions.choice: "스라야에게는 므라야" (Literal), "스라야 가문에는 므라야" (Balanced), through verse 21
decisions.reason: "스라야의 므라야" would read as "Seraiah's son Meraiah"; Literal marks the family with -에게는, Balanced names it as a 가문.

records.literal_gloss: The Levites, in [the] days of Eliashib, Joiada and Johanan and Jaddua, [were] recorded [as] heads of fathers, and the priests, in [the] reign of Darius the Persian.

en.L: The Levites, in the days of Eliashib, Joiada and Johanan and Jaddua, [were] recorded [as] heads of fathers' [houses], and the priests, until the reign of Darius the Persian.
en.B: In the days of Eliashib, Joiada, Johanan and Jaddua, the Levites were recorded by the heads of their fathers' houses, and so were the priests, up to the reign of Darius the Persian.
en.R: The leaders of the Levite families were written down in the records while Eliashib, Joiada, Johanan, and Jaddua were high priests. The priests were written down too, up to the time when Darius the Persian was king.

es.L: Los levitas, en los días de Eliasib, Joiada y Johanán y Jadúa, [fueron] inscritos [como] jefes de [casas] paternas, y los sacerdotes, hasta el reinado de Darío el persa.
es.B: En los días de Eliasib, Joiada, Johanán y Jadúa, los levitas fueron inscritos según los jefes de sus casas paternas, y también los sacerdotes, hasta el reinado de Darío el persa.
es.R: Los jefes de las familias levitas quedaron anotados en los registros mientras Eliasib, Joiada, Johanán y Jadúa eran sumos sacerdotes. También se anotó a los sacerdotes, hasta el tiempo en que Darío el persa era rey.

fr.L: Les Lévites, aux jours d’Éliashib, Yoyada, et Yohanân, et Yaddoua, [furent] inscrits [comme] chefs de [maisons] paternelles, ainsi que les prêtres, jusqu’au règne de Darius le Perse.
fr.B: Au temps d’Éliashib, de Yoyada, de Yohanân et de Yaddoua, les Lévites furent inscrits selon les chefs de leurs familles, et les prêtres aussi, jusqu’au règne de Darius le Perse.
fr.R: Les chefs des familles de Lévites ont été inscrits dans les registres pendant qu’Éliashib, Yoyada, Yohanân et Yaddoua étaient grands prêtres. Les prêtres aussi ont été inscrits, jusqu’à l’époque où Darius le Perse était roi.

sw.L: Walawi, katika siku za Eliashibu, Yoyada na Yohana na Yadua, [waliandikwa kuwa] wakuu wa [nyumba za] baba, na makuhani, mpaka utawala wa Dario Mwajemi.
sw.B: Katika siku za Eliashibu, Yoyada, Yohana na Yadua, Walawi waliandikwa kwa kufuata wakuu wa nyumba za baba zao, na makuhani vilevile, mpaka utawala wa Dario Mwajemi.
sw.R: Viongozi wa jamaa za Walawi waliandikwa katika kumbukumbu wakati Eliashibu, Yoyada, Yohana na Yadua walipokuwa makuhani wakuu. Makuhani nao waliandikwa, mpaka wakati Dario Mwajemi alipokuwa mfalme.

vi.B: Trong thời Ê-li-a-síp, Giô-gia-đa, Giô-ha-nan và Gia-đua, người Lê-vi được ghi vào sổ theo các trưởng tộc của họ, các thầy tế lễ cũng vậy, cho đến triều đại Đa-ri-út người Ba Tư.

ko.L: 레위 사람들은, 엘리아십과 요야다와 요하난과 얏두아의 날들에, 조상[의 가문들]의 우두머리들[로] 기록되었고, 제사장들도 페르시아 사람 다리오의 통치[까지 그러했다].
ko.B: 엘리아십, 요야다, 요하난, 얏두아 때에 레위 사람들은 가문의 우두머리별로 기록되었고, 제사장들도 페르시아 사람 다리오가 다스릴 때까지 그렇게 기록되었다.
ko.R: 엘리아십, 요야다, 요하난, 얏두아가 대제사장이었을 때 레위 가문의 지도자들이 기록에 올랐다. 제사장들도 페르시아 사람 다리오가 왕이었던 때까지 기록에 올랐다.

decisions.choice: Darius the Persian: probably Darius II
decisions.reason: Three Persian kings were named Darius. The high priests named here (verses 10-11) lived after Nehemiah's time, which fits Darius II (423-404 BC). If Jaddua is the high priest of Alexander the Great's time known from later Jewish history, Darius III (336-330 BC) would be meant. The text does not say which.

decisions.choice: in the reign of: up to the reign of
decisions.reason: The preposition can mean "in", "during" or "up to". With a list of four high priests across several generations, the record reached up to the reign of this Darius.

decisions.choice: heads of fathers: heads of fathers' houses
decisions.reason: As in verse 12, the heads of the extended families.

decisions.choice: while ... were high priests
decisions.reason: Readable says who these four men were (verses 10-11).

decisions.choice: "Yohana" for Johanan
decisions.reason: The published Swahili form of Johanan (Jeremiah 40-43); Jehohanan in verse 13 keeps the longer "Yehohanani", as Ezra 10:6 does.

vi.L: Con cái Lê-vi, những người đứng đầu [nhà] tổ phụ, [được] ghi chép trong sách sử ký, cho đến những ngày của Giô-ha-nan con trai Ê-li-a-síp.
vi.B: Con cháu Lê-vi, những trưởng tộc, được ghi vào Sách Sử Ký, cho đến thời Giô-ha-nan con trai Ê-li-a-síp.
vi.R: Những người đứng đầu các gia tộc Lê-vi được ghi trong sổ chính thức ghi lại các biến cố, cho đến thời Giô-ha-nan, cháu nội của Ê-li-a-síp.

ko.L: 레위의 아들들, 곧 조상[의 가문들]의 우두머리들은 엘리아십의 아들 요하난의 날들까지 그날들의 일들의 책에 기록되었다.
ko.B: 레위의 자손들, 곧 가문의 우두머리들은 엘리아십의 아들 요하난 때까지 연대기에 기록되었다.
ko.R: 레위 가문의 지도자들은 엘리아십의 손자 요하난 때까지 공식 기록에 올랐다.

decisions.choice: the scroll of the matters of the days: an official record of events
decisions.reason: "The matters of the days" means the events of each year, a chronicle. It was a record kept in Jerusalem, not necessarily the biblical book of Chronicles, though that book has the same Hebrew name and lists the Levites (1 Chronicles 23-26).

decisions.choice: son of Eliashib: descendant, here grandson
decisions.reason: By verses 10-11 Johanan (or Jonathan) was Eliashib's grandson, son of Joiada. "Son" in Hebrew can name any male descendant.

decisions.choice: Eliashib's grandson
decisions.reason: Readable follows verses 10-11 so the reader is not confused by the two lists.

decisions.choice: "연대기" (Balanced)
decisions.reason: "역대기" is the Korean title of the biblical book of Chronicles; the meaning decision (m1) says this was a record kept in Jerusalem, not necessarily that book, so Balanced uses the general word for a chronicle.

source.text: וְרָאשֵׁ֣י הַ֠לְוִיִּם חֲשַׁבְיָ֨ה שֵֽׁרֵבְיָ֜ה וְיֵשׁ֤וּעַ בֶּן־קַדְמִיאֵל֙ וַאֲחֵיהֶ֣ם לְנֶגְדָּ֔ם לְהַלֵּ֣ל לְהוֹד֔וֹת בְּמִצְוַ֖ת דָּוִ֣יד אִישׁ־הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים מִשְׁמָ֖ר לְעֻמַּ֥ת מִשְׁמָֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] heads of the Levites: Hashabiah, Sherebiah and Jeshua son of Kadmiel, and their brothers opposite them, to praise, to give thanks by [the] command of David, [the] man of God, watch alongside watch.

en.L: And the heads of the Levites were Hashabiah, Sherebiah and Jeshua son of Kadmiel, with their brothers opposite them, to praise and to give thanks, as David the man of God had commanded, watch beside watch.
en.B: The leaders of the Levites were Hashabiah, Sherebiah, and Jeshua son of Kadmiel. Their fellow Levites stood opposite them to praise and give thanks, one group answering the other, as David the man of God had commanded.
en.R: The leaders of the Levites were Hashabiah, Sherebiah, and Jeshua son of Kadmiel. Other Levites stood facing them. Together they praised God and thanked him, one group answering the other, as King David, the man of God, had ordered long before.

es.L: Y los jefes de los levitas [eran] Hasabías, Serebías y Jesúa hijo de Cadmiel, con sus hermanos frente a ellos, para alabar y dar gracias, según el mandato de David, hombre de Dios, turno junto a turno.
es.B: Los jefes de los levitas eran Hasabías, Serebías y Jesúa hijo de Cadmiel. Sus compañeros levitas se colocaban frente a ellos para alabar y dar gracias, un grupo respondiendo al otro, como lo había mandado David, el hombre de Dios.
es.R: Los jefes de los levitas eran Hasabías, Serebías y Jesúa hijo de Cadmiel. Otros levitas se ponían frente a ellos. Juntos alababan a Dios y le daban gracias, un grupo respondiendo al otro, como lo había ordenado mucho antes el rey David, el hombre de Dios.

fr.L: Et les chefs des Lévites [étaient] Hashabia, Shérébia et Yeshoua, fils de Qadmiel, avec leurs frères en face d’eux, pour louer et pour rendre grâce, selon le commandement de David, l’homme de Dieu, garde à côté de garde.
fr.B: Les chefs des Lévites étaient Hashabia, Shérébia et Yeshoua, fils de Qadmiel. Leurs frères lévites se tenaient en face d’eux pour louer et rendre grâce, un groupe répondant à l’autre, comme l’avait ordonné David, l’homme de Dieu.
fr.R: Les chefs des Lévites étaient Hashabia, Shérébia et Yeshoua, fils de Qadmiel. D’autres Lévites se tenaient en face d’eux. Ensemble, ils louaient Dieu et le remerciaient, un groupe répondant à l’autre, comme le roi David, l’homme de Dieu, l’avait ordonné bien longtemps avant.

sw.L: Na wakuu wa Walawi [walikuwa] Hashabia, Sherebia na Yeshua mwana wa Kadmieli, pamoja na ndugu zao kuwakabili, ili kusifu na kushukuru, kwa amri ya Daudi mtu wa Mungu, zamu karibu na zamu.
sw.B: Viongozi wa Walawi walikuwa Hashabia, Sherebia na Yeshua mwana wa Kadmieli. Walawi wenzao walisimama kuwakabili ili kusifu na kushukuru, kundi moja likilijibu jingine, kama Daudi mtu wa Mungu alivyoamuru.
sw.R: Viongozi wa Walawi walikuwa Hashabia, Sherebia na Yeshua mwana wa Kadmieli. Walawi wengine walisimama wakiwatazama. Kwa pamoja walimsifu Mungu na kumshukuru, kundi moja likilijibu jingine, kama Mfalme Daudi, mtu wa Mungu, alivyoamuru zamani.

vi.L: Và những người đứng đầu người Lê-vi [là] Ha-sa-bia, Sê-rê-bia và Giê-sua con trai Cát-mi-ên, cùng anh em họ đối diện với họ, để ca ngợi và cảm tạ, theo lệnh của Đa-vít, người của Đức Chúa Trời, ban bên cạnh ban.
vi.B: Những người lãnh đạo người Lê-vi là Ha-sa-bia, Sê-rê-bia và Giê-sua con trai Cát-mi-ên. Anh em Lê-vi của họ đứng đối diện để ca ngợi và cảm tạ, nhóm này đáp lại nhóm kia, theo như Đa-vít, người của Đức Chúa Trời, đã truyền dạy.
vi.R: Những người lãnh đạo người Lê-vi là Ha-sa-bia, Sê-rê-bia và Giê-sua con trai Cát-mi-ên. Những người Lê-vi khác đứng đối diện với họ. Họ cùng nhau ca ngợi và cảm tạ Đức Chúa Trời, nhóm này đáp lại nhóm kia, đúng như vua Đa-vít, người của Đức Chúa Trời, đã truyền từ lâu.

ko.L: 그리고 레위 사람들의 우두머리들은 하사뱌, 세레뱌, 갓미엘의 아들 예수아[였고], 그들의 형제들은 그들 맞은편에 [서서], 하나님의 사람 다윗의 명령에 따라, 반열 곁에 반열이 찬양하고 감사했다.
ko.B: 레위 사람들의 지도자들은 하사뱌, 세레뱌, 갓미엘의 아들 예수아였다. 그들의 동료 레위 사람들은 하나님의 사람 다윗이 명령한 대로 그들 맞은편에 서서, 한 무리가 다른 무리에 화답하며 찬양하고 감사했다.
ko.R: 레위 사람들의 지도자들은 하사뱌, 세레뱌, 갓미엘의 아들 예수아였다. 다른 레위 사람들은 그들을 마주 보고 섰다. 그들은 오래전에 하나님의 사람 다윗 왕이 명령한 대로, 한 무리가 다른 무리에 화답하며 함께 하나님을 찬양하고 감사드렸다.

decisions.choice: the command of David, the man of God
decisions.reason: 1 Chronicles 23-25 tells how David organized the Levites and the singers into divisions to praise and give thanks. "Man of God" is the title of a prophet; David is called so in 2 Chronicles 8:14 and in verse 36.

decisions.choice: watch beside watch: group answering group
decisions.reason: The words mean one division of singers corresponding to another, the answering song of verse 9.

decisions.choice: Jeshua son of Kadmiel, perhaps Jeshua, Binnui, Kadmiel
decisions.reason: Elsewhere Jeshua, Binnui and Kadmiel are three Levites named together (verse 8; 10:10). The Hebrew word for "son of" and the name Binnui look alike, so the list may first have read "Jeshua, Binnui, Kadmiel". The text as it stands is translated.

decisions.choice: praised God and thanked him; King David ... long before
decisions.reason: Readable names the one praised and says who David was.

source.text: מַתַּנְיָ֧ה וּבַקְבֻּֽקְיָ֛ה עֹבַדְיָ֥ה מְשֻׁלָּ֖ם טַלְמ֣וֹן עַקּ֑וּב שֹׁמְרִ֤ים שֽׁוֹעֲרִים֙ מִשְׁמָ֔ר בַּאֲסֻפֵּ֖י הַשְּׁעָרִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: Mattaniah and Bakbukiah, Obadiah, Meshullam, Talmon, Akkub, keeping guard [as] gatekeepers at the storehouses of the gates.

en.L: Mattaniah and Bakbukiah, Obadiah, Meshullam, Talmon, Akkub [were] gatekeepers keeping guard at the storehouses of the gates.
en.B: Mattaniah, Bakbukiah, Obadiah, Meshullam, Talmon, and Akkub were gatekeepers who stood guard at the storerooms by the gates.
en.R: Mattaniah, Bakbukiah, Obadiah, Meshullam, Talmon, and Akkub were gatekeepers. They guarded the storerooms next to the gates.

es.L: Matanías y Bacbuquías, Abdías, Mesulam, Talmón, Acub [eran] porteros que montaban guardia en los almacenes de las puertas.
es.B: Matanías, Bacbuquías, Abdías, Mesulam, Talmón y Acub eran porteros que hacían guardia en los almacenes junto a las puertas.
es.R: Matanías, Bacbuquías, Abdías, Mesulam, Talmón y Acub eran porteros. Vigilaban los almacenes que estaban junto a las puertas.

fr.L: Mattania et Baqbouqia, Abdias, Meshoullam, Talmôn, Aqqoub [étaient] portiers, montant la garde aux magasins des portes.
fr.B: Mattania, Baqbouqia, Abdias, Meshoullam, Talmôn et Aqqoub étaient portiers et montaient la garde aux magasins près des portes.
fr.R: Mattania, Baqbouqia, Abdias, Meshoullam, Talmôn et Aqqoub étaient portiers. Ils surveillaient les réserves situées près des portes.

sw.L: Matania na Bakbukia, Obadia, Meshulamu, Talmoni, Akubu [walikuwa] mabawabu wakilinda kwenye ghala za malango.
sw.B: Matania, Bakbukia, Obadia, Meshulamu, Talmoni na Akubu walikuwa mabawabu waliolinda ghala zilizokuwa karibu na malango.
sw.R: Matania, Bakbukia, Obadia, Meshulamu, Talmoni na Akubu walikuwa walinzi wa malango. Walilinda ghala zilizokuwa karibu na malango.

vi.L: Mát-ta-nia và Bác-bu-kia, Áp-đia, Mê-su-lam, Thanh-môn, A-cúp [là] những người giữ cổng canh gác tại các kho của các cổng.
vi.B: Mát-ta-nia, Bác-bu-kia, Áp-đia, Mê-su-lam, Thanh-môn và A-cúp là những người giữ cổng, canh gác các kho bên cạnh các cổng.
vi.R: Mát-ta-nia, Bác-bu-kia, Áp-đia, Mê-su-lam, Thanh-môn và A-cúp là những người giữ cổng. Họ canh giữ các nhà kho cạnh các cổng.

ko.L: 맛다냐와 박부갸, 오바댜, 므술람, 달몬, 악굽은 문들의 곳간들을 지키는 문지기들[이었다].
ko.B: 맛다냐, 박부갸, 오바댜, 므술람, 달몬, 악굽은 문 곁에 있는 곳간들을 지키는 문지기들이었다.
ko.R: 맛다냐, 박부갸, 오바댜, 므술람, 달몬, 악굽은 문지기였다. 그들은 문 옆에 있는 창고들을 지켰다.

decisions.choice: who the gatekeepers were
decisions.reason: Mattaniah, Bakbukiah and probably Obadiah were singers (verses 8-9; 11:17), while Talmon and Akkub were gatekeepers (11:19). The verse may join two groups, the first three closing the singers of verse 24 and the last three being gatekeepers, or these men may have served in both ways. The Hebrew sets them in one list.

decisions.choice: the storehouses of the gates
decisions.reason: Store rooms built at or beside the temple gates, where the gifts of verse 44 were kept (compare 1 Chronicles 26:15).

source.text: אֵ֕לֶּה בִּימֵ֛י יוֹיָקִ֥ים בֶּן־יֵשׁ֖וּעַ בֶּן־יוֹצָדָ֑ק וּבִימֵי֙ נְחֶמְיָ֣ה הַפֶּחָ֔ה וְעֶזְרָ֥א הַכֹּהֵ֖ן הַסּוֹפֵֽר׃פ

records.literal_gloss: These [were] in [the] days of Joiakim son of Jeshua son of Jozadak, and in [the] days of Nehemiah the governor and Ezra the priest, the scribe.

en.L: These [were] in the days of Joiakim son of Jeshua son of Jozadak, and in the days of Nehemiah the governor and of Ezra the priest, the scribe.
en.B: These served in the days of Joiakim son of Jeshua son of Jozadak, and in the days of Nehemiah the governor and of Ezra the priest and scribe.
en.R: These men served when Joiakim son of Jeshua, son of Jozadak, was high priest, and when Nehemiah was governor and Ezra was priest and teacher of the law.

es.L: Estos [fueron] en los días de Joiacim hijo de Jesúa, hijo de Josadac, y en los días de Nehemías el gobernador y de Esdras el sacerdote, el escriba.
es.B: Estos sirvieron en los días de Joiacim hijo de Jesúa, hijo de Josadac, y en los días de Nehemías el gobernador y de Esdras, sacerdote y escriba.
es.R: Estos hombres sirvieron cuando Joiacim hijo de Jesúa, hijo de Josadac, era sumo sacerdote, y cuando Nehemías era gobernador y Esdras era sacerdote y maestro de la ley.

fr.L: Ceux-ci [furent] aux jours de Yoyaqim, fils de Yeshoua, fils de Yotsadaq, et aux jours de Néhémie le gouverneur et d’Esdras le prêtre, le scribe.
fr.B: Ceux-ci servirent au temps de Yoyaqim, fils de Yeshoua, fils de Yotsadaq, et au temps de Néhémie le gouverneur et d’Esdras, prêtre et scribe.
fr.R: Ces hommes ont servi quand Yoyaqim, fils de Yeshoua, fils de Yotsadaq, était grand prêtre, et quand Néhémie était gouverneur et qu’Esdras était prêtre et spécialiste de la Loi.

sw.L: Hawa [walikuwa] katika siku za Yoyakimu mwana wa Yeshua mwana wa Yosadaki, na katika siku za Nehemia liwali na za Ezra kuhani, mwandishi.
sw.B: Hawa walihudumu katika siku za Yoyakimu mwana wa Yeshua mwana wa Yosadaki, na katika siku za Nehemia liwali na za Ezra kuhani na mwandishi.
sw.R: Watu hawa walihudumu wakati Yoyakimu mwana wa Yeshua, mwana wa Yosadaki, alipokuwa kuhani mkuu, na wakati Nehemia alipokuwa liwali na Ezra alipokuwa kuhani na mwalimu wa sheria.

vi.L: Những người này [ở] trong những ngày của Giô-gia-kim con trai Giê-sua con trai Giô-xa-đác, và trong những ngày của Nê-hê-mi, tổng đốc, và của E-xơ-ra, thầy tế lễ, thầy thông giáo.
vi.B: Những người này phục vụ trong thời Giô-gia-kim con trai Giê-sua con trai Giô-xa-đác, và trong thời tổng đốc Nê-hê-mi và E-xơ-ra, thầy tế lễ và thầy thông giáo.
vi.R: Những người này phục vụ khi Giô-gia-kim con trai Giê-sua, con trai Giô-xa-đác, làm thầy tế lễ thượng phẩm, và khi Nê-hê-mi làm tổng đốc, còn E-xơ-ra làm thầy tế lễ và thầy dạy luật pháp.

ko.L: 이들은 요사닥의 아들 예수아의 아들 요야김의 날들과, 총독 느헤미야와 제사장이며 서기관인 에스라의 날들에 [있었다].
ko.B: 이들은 요사닥의 아들 예수아의 아들 요야김 때와, 총독 느헤미야와 제사장이자 서기관인 에스라 때에 섬겼다.
ko.R: 이 사람들은 요사닥의 손자이자 예수아의 아들인 요야김이 대제사장이었을 때, 그리고 느헤미야가 총독이고 에스라가 제사장이자 율법 선생이었을 때 섬겼다.

decisions.choice: the time span of the lists
decisions.reason: Joiakim was high priest in the generation after the return (verse 10); Nehemiah came as governor in 445 BC (2:1; 5:14), and Ezra had come thirteen years earlier (Ezra 7:7-8). The verse closes the lists of verses 1-25 by tying them to these leaders.

decisions.choice: the scribe: an expert in the law of Moses
decisions.reason: Ezra is called a scribe skilled in the law of Moses (Ezra 7:6, 11). The word means more than a copyist: one who studies and teaches the law.

decisions.choice: These served
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has no verb; "served" says in what sense the people of the lists were "in the days of" these leaders.

decisions.choice: teacher of the law
decisions.reason: Readable's wording for Ezra the scribe, as in Ezra 7:6.

source.text: וּבַחֲנֻכַּ֞ת חוֹמַ֣ת יְרוּשָׁלִַ֗ם בִּקְשׁ֤וּ אֶת־הַלְוִיִּם֙ מִכָּל־מְק֣וֹמֹתָ֔ם לַהֲבִיאָ֖ם לִֽירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם לַעֲשֹׂ֨ת חֲנֻכָּ֤ה וְשִׂמְחָה֙ וּבְתוֹד֣וֹת וּבְשִׁ֔יר מְצִלְתַּ֖יִם נְבָלִ֥ים וּבְכִנֹּרֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: And at [the] dedication of [the] wall of Jerusalem they sought the Levites from all their places to bring them to Jerusalem to make [the] dedication and joy, and with thanksgivings and with song, cymbals, harps and with lyres.

en.L: And at the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem they sought the Levites from all their places, to bring them to Jerusalem to hold the dedication with joy, and with thanksgivings and with song, [with] cymbals, harps and lyres.
en.B: At the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem, the Levites were sought out from all the places where they lived and brought to Jerusalem to celebrate the dedication with joy, with songs of thanksgiving, and with the music of cymbals, harps, and lyres.
en.R: When the time came to dedicate the wall of Jerusalem, the people looked for the Levites in all the places where they lived and brought them to Jerusalem. They wanted to celebrate the dedication with joy, singing songs of thanks and playing cymbals, harps, and lyres.

decisions.choice: dedication: the ceremony that gave the finished wall to God's use
decisions.reason: The same word is used for the dedication of the altar (Numbers 7:84), of Solomon's temple (2 Chronicles 7:9) and of the rebuilt temple (Ezra 6:16-17). The wall was finished in fifty-two days (6:15); this ceremony follows, perhaps some time later, after the repopulation of the city (11:1-2).

decisions.choice: cymbals, harps, lyres: the instruments of temple song
decisions.reason: These three are named together for the Levites' music in David's arrangements (1 Chronicles 15:16; 25:1). The harp and lyre were both stringed instruments; their exact shapes are not certain.

decisions.choice: they sought: an impersonal subject
decisions.reason: The verb has no named subject; the leaders of the city, or the people as a whole, sent for the Levites. Many Levites lived in towns outside Jerusalem (11:3, 36).

decisions.choice: hold the dedication with joy (Literal); celebrate the dedication with joy (Balanced)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "to make dedication and joy" means a dedication celebrated with gladness; Literal and Balanced join the two words.

source.text: וַיֵּאָ֣סְפ֔וּ בְּנֵ֖י הַמְשֹׁרְרִ֑ים וּמִן־הַכִּכָּר֙ סְבִיב֣וֹת יְרוּשָׁלִַ֔ם וּמִן־חַצְרֵ֖י נְטֹפָתִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And were gathered the sons of the singers, both from the circle around Jerusalem and from [the] villages of [the] Netophathite[s],

en.L: And the sons of the singers were gathered, both from the circle around Jerusalem and from the villages of the Netophathites,
en.B: And the sons of the singers gathered, both from the district around Jerusalem and from the villages of the Netophathites,
en.R: The singers also came together. They came from the area around Jerusalem, from the villages near Netophah,

decisions.choice: the sons of the singers: the members of the singers' guild
decisions.reason: "Sons of" a group means those who belong to it, as "sons of the prophets" means prophets (2 Kings 2:3). The singers were Levite families whose office passed from father to son (1 Chronicles 25).

decisions.choice: the district around Jerusalem; Netophah
decisions.reason: The "circle" is the ring of land and villages around the city. Netophah was a village near Bethlehem; its people returned from exile (Ezra 2:22) and Levites lived in its villages (1 Chronicles 9:16).

decisions.choice: the singers (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps "the sons of the singers" so the guild idiom stays visible; Readable says simply "the singers".

decisions.choice: Beth-gilgal, Geba, Azmaveth: villages near Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Geba and Azmaveth lay a few miles north and northeast of Jerusalem in the land of Benjamin (Ezra 2:24, 26; 11:31). Beth-gilgal ("house of Gilgal") is probably a Gilgal near Jerusalem; which one is not certain.

decisions.reason: The clause explains the list: the singers lived in villages of their own around the city, not in Jerusalem itself.

decisions.choice: purified: made ritually clean for worship
decisions.reason: Before a holy act the priests and Levites made themselves clean, by washing, by keeping away from what defiles, and by offerings (Exodus 19:10-15; Numbers 8:5-22; Ezra 6:20). The text does not say how the gates and the wall were purified; the point is that the whole city was made fit to be given to God.

decisions.choice: so that all of it was fit to be given to God
decisions.reason: Readable adds the purpose, which the dedication of verse 27 implies.

en.L: And I brought the princes of Judah up on top of the wall, and I appointed two great thanksgiving [choirs] and processions; [one went] to the right on top of the wall toward the Dung Gate.
en.B: And I brought the officials of Judah up on top of the wall, and I appointed two great thanksgiving choirs to walk in procession. One went to the right on top of the wall, toward the Dung Gate.
en.R: Then I had the leaders of Judah climb up on top of the wall. I put together two large choirs to give thanks to God as they marched. The first went to the right along the top of the wall, toward the Dung Gate.

decisions.choice: I: Nehemiah's own account begins again
decisions.reason: From here to the end of the book Nehemiah tells the story in the first person, as in chapters 1-7. The lists of chapters 11-12 stand between.

decisions.choice: thanksgiving choirs and processions
decisions.reason: "Thanksgivings" here means choirs that sang thanks (also verses 38 and 40). The next word, found only here, comes from the verb "to walk": processions. Some read the line as "two great choirs, and the procession [of the first went] to the right". Either way two choirs walked on the wall in opposite directions and met at the temple (verse 40).

decisions.choice: to the right, toward the Dung Gate: south
decisions.reason: The Dung Gate was at the southern end of the city (2:13; 3:13-14). The choirs probably set out from the west side, near the Valley Gate, so the first went south and east and the second north (verses 38-39).

decisions.choice: princes (Literal); officials (Balanced); leaders (Readable)
decisions.reason: The project's wording for this word for leaders.

decisions.choice: one went; The first went
decisions.reason: The Hebrew does not say "one"; the verse goes on to describe the route of the first choir, as verse 38 describes the second.

decisions.choice: sons of the priests: priests
decisions.reason: "Sons of the priests" means members of the priestly families, priests themselves; the trumpets were the priests' instruments (Numbers 10:8; Ezra 3:10).

decisions.choice: Zechariah, a descendant of Asaph, leads the Levite musicians
decisions.reason: Asaph was one of David's chief singers (1 Chronicles 16:5; 25:1), so Zechariah was a Levite, not a priest. The trumpeters' names are not given here (compare verse 41); Zechariah heads the Levite musicians of verse 36. Mattaniah is probably the singer of 11:17 and 12:8.

decisions.choice: Then came Zechariah (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable separate Zechariah from the priests with trumpets, following the meaning decision; Literal keeps the colon of the bare list.

decisions.choice: a descendant of Asaph through ...
decisions.reason: Readable turns the chain of six names around so the famous ancestor comes first.

en.B: and his brothers Shemaiah, Azarel, Milalai, Gilalai, Maai, Nethanel, Judah, and Hanani, with the musical instruments of David the man of God. Ezra the scribe walked in front of them.
en.R: and his fellow Levites Shemaiah, Azarel, Milalai, Gilalai, Maai, Nethanel, Judah, and Hanani. They played the kinds of instruments that King David, the man of God, had used for worship. Ezra, the teacher of the law, led this group.

decisions.choice: the instruments of David
decisions.reason: David is remembered as the one who brought instruments into the worship of God (1 Chronicles 23:5; 2 Chronicles 29:26-27; Amos 6:5).

decisions.choice: Ezra the scribe at the head of the first choir
decisions.reason: Ezra led one procession and Nehemiah followed the other (verse 38), so the two leaders of chapters 8-10 appear together again (8:9).

decisions.choice: teacher of the law
decisions.reason: Readable's wording for Ezra the scribe, as in Ezra 7:6.

en.L: And at the Gate of the Fountain, and straight before them, they went up on the steps of the City of David, at the ascent of the wall, above the house of David, and to the Gate of the Water [on the] east.
en.B: At the Fountain Gate they went straight up the steps of the City of David, where the wall goes up, above the house of David, and on to the Water Gate on the east.
en.R: At the Fountain Gate they went straight ahead and climbed the steps that lead up to the City of David. They followed the wall as it rose, past the place above David's palace, and went on as far as the Water Gate on the east side of the city.

decisions.choice: the route of the first choir
decisions.reason: The Fountain Gate, the steps going down from the City of David and the Water Gate are all named in the account of the rebuilding (3:15, 26). The choir walked north along the eastern side of the old City of David toward the temple.

decisions.choice: straight before them: straight ahead
decisions.reason: The phrase means going straight on without turning aside. Some join it with the preceding words: "at the Fountain Gate, in front of them".

decisions.choice: the house of David: David's palace
decisions.reason: The royal house David built (2 Samuel 5:11), by then perhaps only its ruins or its site. The wall ran above it.

decisions.choice: past the place above David's palace
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the sense that the wall passed above the palace site, without deciding whether the palace still stood.

decisions.reason: The word usually means "in front of" or "facing"; here it means the direction opposite to the first choir, which went to the right (verse 31). The second choir went north along the western wall.

decisions.choice: the Tower of the Ovens and the Broad Wall
decisions.reason: Both are named in the account of the rebuilding of the west and north walls (3:8, 11).

decisions.choice: to the left
decisions.reason: Readable adds what "opposite" means here, from verse 31.

decisions.choice: the route of the second choir along the north wall
decisions.reason: These gates and towers are named in the account of the rebuilding of the north side of the city (3:1-6; the Ephraim Gate in 8:16 and 2 Kings 14:13). The procession ended near the temple, at its northern side.

decisions.choice: the Jeshanah Gate: perhaps the Old Gate
decisions.reason: The name can mean "the old [gate]", or it may name the gate on the road to the town of Jeshanah (2 Chronicles 13:19). The same gate is named in 3:6.

decisions.choice: the Gate of the Guard
decisions.reason: This gate is named only here; it was probably a temple gate near the place where the guard was kept (compare "the court of the guard", 3:25). Its site is not known.

decisions.choice: The choir stopped
decisions.reason: Readable names the subject of "they stood", the second choir.

decisions.choice: officials

decisions.choice: God's temple

decisions.choice: the priests with trumpets in the second procession

decisions.reason: These eight are probably the Levite singers of the second choir, matching Zechariah's group in verse 36; the verse then turns to the singing.

decisions.reason: The verb means "caused to be heard", with "their voice" understood (1 Chronicles 15:16, 19, 28): the singers sang out so as to be heard.

decisions.choice: the overseer: the one in charge
decisions.reason: The word means an appointed overseer (11:9, 14, 22). Izrahiah directed the singers.

decisions.choice: God had made them rejoice
decisions.reason: The joy is credited to God as its giver, as at the Feast of Booths (8:10, 17) and the dedication of the temple (Ezra 6:22). The words for joy and rejoicing come five times in this one verse.

decisions.choice: the women and the children
decisions.reason: The whole community took part, as at the reading of the law (8:2-3) and the pledge (10:29).

decisions.choice: heard from far away
decisions.reason: The same words describe the shouting at the founding of the temple, when weeping and joy were mixed (Ezra 3:13). Here only joy is heard.

source.text: וַיִּפָּקְד֣וּ בַיּוֹם֩ הַה֨וּא אֲנָשִׁ֜ים עַל־הַנְּשָׁכ֗וֹת לָא֨וֹצָר֥וֹת לַתְּרוּמוֹת֮ לָרֵאשִׁ֣ית וְלַמַּֽעַשְׂרוֹת֒ לִכְנ֨וֹס בָּהֶ֜ם לִשְׂדֵ֤י הֶעָרִים֙ מְנָא֣וֹת הַתּוֹרָ֔ה לַכֹּהֲנִ֖ים וְלַלְוִיִּ֑ם כִּ֚י שִׂמְחַ֣ת יְהוּדָ֔ה עַל־הַכֹּהֲנִ֥ים וְעַל־הַלְוִיִּ֖ם הָעֹמְדִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And were appointed on that day men over the chambers for the stores, for the contributions, for the first [fruits] and for the tithes, to gather into them, from [the] fields of the cities, the portions of the law for priests and for Levites; for [the] joy of Judah [was] over the priests and over the Levites who stood.

en.L: And on that day men were appointed over the chambers for the stores, for the contributions, for the first [fruits] and for the tithes, to gather into them from the fields of the cities the portions of the law for [the] priests and for [the] Levites; for the joy of Judah [was] over the priests and over the Levites who stood.
en.B: And on that day men were appointed over the chambers for the stores, for the contributions, for the firstfruits and for the tithes, to gather into them from the fields of the towns the portions required by the law for the priests and for the Levites; for Judah rejoiced over the priests and the Levites who stood to serve.
en.R: That same day men were put in charge of the storerooms where the people's gifts were kept: the first part of each harvest and the tenth part of all the crops. These men had to collect from the fields around the towns the share that God's law said should go to the priests and Levites. The people of Judah were glad because the priests and Levites were serving God.

decisions.choice: contributions, firstfruits, tithes
decisions.reason: The contributions were gifts set apart for the priests (Numbers 18:8-19); the firstfruits were the first of each harvest (Numbers 18:12-13); the tithes were a tenth of the produce, given to the Levites (Numbers 18:21-24). The people had pledged to bring all three (10:36-40).

decisions.choice: the portions of the law: the shares the law assigned
decisions.reason: The law of Moses set out what was due to the priests and Levites; these men collected it.

decisions.choice: for Judah rejoiced: the reason for the arrangement
decisions.reason: Because the people were glad of the priests and Levites serving, they made sure their shares were collected. "Who stood" means who stood to serve before God (Deuteronomy 10:8; 18:7).

decisions.choice: the first part of each harvest and the tenth part of all the crops
decisions.reason: Readable explains firstfruits and tithes in plain words.

decisions.choice: who stood to serve
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the Hebrew "stood" and adds the purpose that the phrase means.

records.literal_gloss: And they kept [the] charge of their God and [the] charge of the purification, and the singers and the gatekeepers, according to [the] command of David [and] Solomon his son.

en.L: And they kept the charge of their God and the charge of the purification, and the singers and the gatekeepers [too], according to the command of David [and] Solomon his son.
en.B: They performed the service of their God and the service of purification, and so did the singers and the gatekeepers, as David and his son Solomon had commanded.
en.R: The priests and Levites did the work God had given them, including the work of keeping things ritually clean. The singers and gatekeepers did their work too, just as King David and his son Solomon had ordered.

decisions.choice: the charge: the duty entrusted to them
decisions.reason: The word means what one is charged to guard or carry out, the set duties of the priests and Levites (Numbers 3:7-8; 1 Chronicles 23:32). Purification was one of the Levites' tasks (1 Chronicles 23:28).

decisions.choice: the command of David and of Solomon
decisions.reason: David arranged the Levites, singers and gatekeepers (1 Chronicles 23-26), and Solomon put the arrangement into practice in the temple (2 Chronicles 8:14).

decisions.choice: and the singers and the gatekeepers: also subjects
decisions.reason: The singers and gatekeepers are added to "they", the priests and Levites of verse 44: they too did their duty.

source.text: כִּֽי־בִימֵ֥י דָוִ֛יד וְאָסָ֖ף מִקֶּ֑דֶם רָאשֵׁי֙ הַמְשֹׁ֣רְרִ֔ים וְשִׁיר־תְּהִלָּ֥ה וְהֹד֖וֹת לֵֽאלֹהִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: For in [the] days of David and Asaph from of old [were] heads of the singers and song of praise and thanksgiving to God.

en.L: For in the days of David and Asaph, from of old, [there were] heads of the singers, and song of praise and thanksgiving to God.
en.B: For long ago, in the days of David and Asaph, there were leaders of the singers, and there were songs of praise and thanksgiving to God.
en.R: Long ago, in the days of King David and of Asaph, there had been leaders over the singers, and songs of praise and thanks to God.

decisions.choice: David and Asaph
decisions.reason: Asaph was David's chief singer (1 Chronicles 16:5, 7), and twelve psalms bear his name (Psalm 50 and Psalms 73-83). The verse explains why the singers had a right to their portions: their office went back to David.

decisions.choice: leaders, as the text is read
decisions.reason: The written text has "leader" (singular), perhaps meaning Asaph as the head; the text is read, as noted in the margin (the qere), as "leaders". This translation follows the reading, as the source data does. The sense hardly changes.

source.text: וְכָל־יִשְׂרָאֵל֩ בִּימֵ֨י זְרֻבָּבֶ֜ל וּבִימֵ֣י נְחֶמְיָ֗ה נֹֽתְנִ֛ים מְנָי֛וֹת הַמְשֹׁרְרִ֥ים וְהַשֹּׁעֲרִ֖ים דְּבַר־י֣וֹם בְּיוֹמ֑וֹ וּמַקְדִּשִׁים֙ לַלְוִיִּ֔ם וְהַלְוִיִּ֔ם מַקְדִּשִׁ֖ים לִבְנֵ֥י אַהֲרֹֽן׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And all Israel in [the] days of Zerubbabel and in [the] days of Nehemiah [were] giving [the] portions of the singers and the gatekeepers, [the] matter of a day in its day; and [they were] setting apart for the Levites, and the Levites setting apart for [the] sons of Aaron.

en.L: And all Israel in the days of Zerubbabel and in the days of Nehemiah [were] giving the portions of the singers and the gatekeepers, the matter of a day in its day; and [they were] setting apart for the Levites, and the Levites setting apart for the sons of Aaron.
en.B: In the days of Zerubbabel and in the days of Nehemiah, all Israel gave the singers and the gatekeepers their daily portions. They set apart what was due to the Levites, and the Levites set apart what was due to the descendants of Aaron.
en.R: When Zerubbabel and later Nehemiah were leaders, all the people of Israel gave the singers and gatekeepers what they needed each day. They set aside a share for the Levites, and the Levites set aside part of what they received for the priests, Aaron's descendants.

decisions.choice: setting apart: giving as holy
decisions.reason: The verb means "to make holy", here to set aside a gift as belonging to God and so to his servants. The Levites in turn gave a tenth of their tithe to the priests (Numbers 18:26-28; Nehemiah 10:39).

decisions.choice: the matter of a day in its day: each day's due
decisions.reason: A set phrase for a daily allowance (Exodus 5:13; Ezra 3:4).

decisions.choice: from Zerubbabel to Nehemiah
decisions.reason: The verse sums up the century since the return (verse 1) as a time when the gifts were faithfully given, which sets up the contrast of 13:10, where Nehemiah finds them neglected.

decisions.choice: the priests, Aaron's descendants
decisions.reason: Readable says who the sons of Aaron were.
